title: Is the student right about these two numbers?
description: Harpreet compares two shop bills. A student says the first bill is greater because its first digit is bigger. The video counts the digits to settle it.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the digits first, because the number with more digits is greater. Watch for comparing the first digits of numbers that have different lengths.

source: Let Us Do 4, the student's claim
video_script.why: The child compares numbers of the same length but has not yet met a pair with different numbers of digits.
video_script.substitution: Count the digits of each number first, and only compare digit by digit when the counts match.
video_script.anchor: Harpreet comparing two shop bills at a stationery shop
video_script.wrong_answer: the student is correct, because nine is greater than four
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu agrees with the student because nine is greater than four. He compares the first digits, but the two numbers have different numbers of digits, so the first digits are in different places.
video_script.payoff_line: the student compared digits that sit in different places

final_answer.value: The student is not correct: 9,990 < 49,014, because 49,014 has more digits
final_answer.spoken: the student is not correct, because nine thousand nine hundred and ninety is less than forty-nine thousand and fourteen, which has more digits

maths_rules: bills: 9,990 has 4 digits (9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 0 ones); 49,014 has 5 digits (4 ten thousands, 9 thousands, 0 hundreds, 1 ten, 4 ones)
the student compared 9 with 4, but the 9 in 9,990 is in the thousands place and the 4 in 49,014 is in the ten thousands place
a 5 digit number is at least 10,000 and a 4 digit number is at most 9,999; so any 5 digit number is greater than any 4 digit number
answer: The student is not correct: 9,990 < 49,014, because 49,014 has more digits
video_script.design: Exercise: judge a claim about two numbers. Hint: count the digits of each number. The two bills stay on the stage and the digit counts are written under them.

<bookmark mark='ask'/>A student says the first bill is greater because its first digit is greater. Is the student right? Say why, or why not.
